steps.headline: Your copy edits, in place — and the switch still asks before it turns the buddy on.
steps.changed: "that is why the buddy sits wherever it lands" is gone. "Without this helper, the buddy floater cannot be enabled." now closes the first paragraph.
steps.notice: The popup states plainly that there is no buddy without the helper, so Not now reads as a real choice rather than a mystery.
steps.risk: None known. This is the wording you dictated; check it reads the way you meant.

steps.headline: The "Pin buddy above other windows" switch is gone completely, as you asked — not just once the helper is installed.
steps.changed: The row, its saved preference in this panel, and its error hint are all removed. The popup is now a single row in every state.
steps.notice: One switch where there were two. The buddy is always pinned above other windows when it is on.
steps.risk: The main-process preference and the KWin code behind it still exist and still work — only this control is gone. If you ever want an unpinned buddy again it is a new control, not a revert.

steps.headline: "Not yet supported" rather than a flat no — and the explanation now gets the full width.
steps.changed: Wording is "Not yet supported on this desktop", leading the description instead of sitting in a narrow right-hand column, which had squeezed the text into six cramped lines.
steps.notice: Three tidy lines instead of a ribbon, and the wording implies this may change rather than closing the door.
steps.risk: "Not yet" is a soft promise. Nobody is working on GNOME support today, and nothing here creates a plan for it — if that matters, the roadmap is where it should be written down, not implied by a settings row.
